title: Seaborn: statistical graphics

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?

Seaborn was created under Michael Waskom's leadership to make statistical graphics easier to explore. It works naturally with pandas tables and builds on Matplotlib, which handles rendering and file output. Its dataset-oriented API maps columns to color, groups, and statistical summaries.
PURPOSE AND SETUP
A plot helps compare numbers quickly and spot trends or unusual measurements. Matplotlib and Seaborn create plots that can be shown on screen or saved to a file. Install the examples with
python -m pip install matplotlib seaborn pandas
RUNNABLE EXAMPLES
Example 1: compare average scores across classes with a bar chart.
QUESTION: What plot will this code create? Predict first, then run it.

spans.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns

scores = pd.DataFrame({
    'class': ['A', 'A', 'B', 'B', 'C', 'C'],
    'score': [70, 80, 75, 85, 82, 88],
})
sns.set_theme(style='whitegrid')
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
sns.barplot(data=scores, x='class', y='score', errorbar=None, ax=ax)
ax.set(title='Average score by class', xlabel='Class', ylabel='Score')
plt.show()
A bar chart titled "Average score by class" opens.
